content:
mika: Quick report: onboarding sample-app (node) behaves differently vs curl in private-dedicated. SDK v1.5.0 drops a header and renames a param; REST works.
joel: Details?
mika: curl I used:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant: team-a" -d '{"model":"search-v2","q":"foo","use_cache":false}' https://private.api.redwood.local/v1/search
```
anya: And SDK call?
mika: Node call:
```js
client.search.create({ model: 'search-v2', q: 'foo', useCache: false })
```
joel: Two issues: (1) SDK sends X-Tenant as X-Tenant-Id in private env (legacy rename). Private gateway rejects it. (2) SDK camelCases useCache -> useCache, while private service expects use_cache. Public proxy accepts both so this slipped by.
anya: Oof. Consequences: missing tenant header caused 403, and missing use_cache caused stale results (defaults to true).
mika: Repro in CI: curl -> 200, SDK -> 403; payload mismatch logged.
joel: Action items: 1) Short-term: doc workaround to set REDWOOD_HEADER_TENANT=X-Tenant in env or set custom headers in client config. 2) Patch SDK serializer to preserve snake_case for known fields on server-critical endpoints (search, rerank, embeddings). 3) Revert the legacy header rename for private by default.
anya: Also add a regression test that compares raw JSON sent by SDK vs expected REST body for quickstart flows.
devex-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/9444 and assigned to joel.
mika: Thanks — I'll update the sample-app README with explicit headers and param-shape notes until the fix lands.
